title: Inter-Dominion Agreement on the Recovery of Abducted Women, 1947
summary: On 6 December 1947 an Inter-Dominion Conference at Lahore had India and Pakistan agree to find and return women and children abducted during the violence of Partition. The accord in practice covered women only and called for recovery whatever the women wanted, a feature later criticised by historians. It led to the Indian Abducted Persons (Recovery and Restoration) Act of 1949.

uncertainty.note: Two sources give the same day.

as_recorded.value: On December 6, 1947, at the Inter-Dominion Conference in Lahore

where.historical_name: Lahore, Punjab, in the newly created Dominion of Pakistan

importance.justification: It set the first joint India–Pakistan machinery for recovering abducted women, whose treatment later became a major subject of Partition scholarship.

audience_note: Concerns the abduction and sexual violence suffered by women during Partition, and a recovery policy that overrode their own wishes.

sources.title: How 2 women led the mission to rescue 30,000 abductees

reviewer_note: Least sure of the place: only the Tribune names Lahore as the venue; the Graduate Institute says only that the treaty was signed 6 December 1947. The Nehru Archive page was blocked and not opened.
